scope.summary: This standard specifies requirements for aluminium and aluminium alloy foil stock in the form of cold-rolled coils, designed as feedstock for the downstream manufacture of thin aluminium foil of various gauges. It covers chemical composition, mechanical properties, dimensional tolerances, and general technical delivery requirements.

certification_and_marking.standard_type: Product Specification (Metallurgical Engineering / Wrought Light Metals)
certification_and_marking.certification_status: Voluntary Quality and Performance Certification. Unlike builders hardware or metal packaging containers which are under strict statutory Quality Control Orders (QCOs), industrial aluminium foil stock under IS 10257 : 1982 is certified on a voluntary basis. Conforming manufacturers are eligible to apply for a BIS license to use the Standard Mark (ISI Mark) under Scheme-I of Schedule-II of the BIS (Conformity Assessment) Regulations, 2018. Compliance is routinely mandated inside public and private sector heavy industrial and metallurgical rolling mill supply contracts. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to industrial raw aluminium coils.

requirements.detail: Every commercial tag or label attached to bundles/coils of aluminium foil stock, along with the accompanying test certificate, must bear the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) along with the manufacturer's registered licence number (CM/L).

The foil stock must be manufactured from high-purity aluminium or wrought aluminium alloys (such as designations 19000, 19500, 1200, 1235, or 8011) ensuring low iron, silicon, and copper impurity limits to prevent tearing during high-speed rolling into micro-gauges.
Foil stock must be supplied as continuous, solid cold-rolled coils, wound tightly with uniform tension to prevent telescoping or collapse of the inner core during transit and uncoiling.

Stock is typically supplied in one of the standard tempers as specified by the purchaser (such as O - Annealed or H14 - Half-hard) in accordance with temper standards to ensure appropriate starting ductility.

The surface must be clean, smooth, bright, and completely free from physical defects such as edge cracks, laminations, pinholes, slivers, deep scratch marks, corrosion, or heavy surface oxidation which could cause tearing or localized punctures during foil-rolling.

Wrought test specimens must satisfy mechanical limits (such as ultimate tensile strength and minimum elongation percentage) to ensure the sheet can sustain the severe tensions experienced in high-speed, downstream multi-stand rolling mills.

If any test specimen fails to comply with mechanical or chemical limits, a retest is permitted: two additional samples must be drawn from the same lot. The lot is accepted if both retests pass, and is rejected if either retest fails.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 10257 : 1982 is the national Indian Standard specification governing aluminium and aluminium alloy foil stock in the form of continuous, tightly wound cold-rolled coils. This stock serves as the essential raw material (feedstock) for foil-rolling mills, which cold-roll the metal down to extremely thin gauges (such as household foils, food-packaging wraps, and pharmaceutical laminates). Certified on a voluntary basis under the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) scheme, the standard enforces strict chemical and physical boundaries to prevent tearing or puncturing during high-speed rolling. It regulates metallurgical purity (restricting impurities like silicon and iron), dimensional tolerances under IS 10259, surface cleanliness (requiring freedom from edge cracks and surface oxidation), and mechanical ductility (tensile strength and elongation) based on temper designations (O or H14) per IS 5052.
